title: Stay with client-side pre-push hook enforcement; decline CI required-status-check migration; optional detective (non-required) CI replay of CHECK 1/2/3
summary: DIRECTIVE-20260712-002 asked for a cost/benefit study of migrating PROP-121/127 pre-push hook enforcement from client-side to CI required-status-checks. Full study at monitor/tinker/reports/ci-hook-migration-study-2026-07-12.md. Verdict: the trade does not warrant migration. Marginal detection gain is exactly one incident class (hook-install-skip, observed once: eab98c5 2026-07-01); required-status-checks cannot pass on direct pushes, forcing a PR-based re-architecture of ~12 agent push paths whose new improvisation surface plausibly exceeds the risk retired; and 'required' checks are fail-CLOSED by platform construction - a broken workflow blocks all pushes to main until the operator intervenes, killing FUSE-to-git rescue for hours-to-days, which is precisely the PROP-051 disaster-class property (2026-05-21 recovery used direct pushes + Git Data API force-reset, both of which strict enforcement blocks or slows).

analysis.q1_push_cadence: ~27.9 commits/day (404 commits 2026-06-30..07-14), ~15-25 push events/day; 70% in UTC 01-05 window, 21% at UTC 09.
analysis.q2_latency: Real cost is not 30-60s: required checks reject direct pushes outright (no check has run on a new commit), forcing PR flow at 1-3+ min/push plus stale-base retry races in burst windows (139/404 inter-commit gaps <120s). PAT subtlety: agents push with the operator PAT; bypass-actor config either swallows enforcement (agents bypass too) or blocks the operator's own disaster-recovery path.

2026-07-10_status_json_chimera.client_side: NOT caught (PROP-130 canary is the instrument)

analysis.q4_fail_open: Unpreservable in required-CI: 'required' and 'fail-open' contradict at platform level. Escape hatches (ruleset bypass actor; API enforcement=disabled) both bound unblock time by operator availability, during which workspace-sync FUSE-to-git rescue is dead. Client-side CHECK 3 fail-open costs one WARN line and zero availability. CI migration also adds a hard runtime dependency on GitHub Actions where none exists today.

phase_1_optional_detective_ci.design: Add a second job 'push-lint-replay' to the existing .github/workflows/ci.yml (on: push to main). Steps: checkout with fetch-depth 50; run a thin adapter (monitor/scripts/ci-lint-replay.js, ~30 lines) that feeds the range ${{ github.event.before }}..${{ github.sha }} into the CHECK 1/2/3 logic of lint-workspace-sync-push.js; exit nonzero on violation. NOT added to any ruleset as required - a red X + GitHub notification email is the whole mechanism. Zero push latency (post-land), zero fail-closed risk, converts the install-skip class from silent-until-integrity-run to alarmed-within-~2-min.
phase_1_optional_detective_ci.constraint_compliance: Does not modify rulesets 18827810/11/12; does not disable client-side hooks; not a wholesale migration.

flip_triggers_to_revisit_ship: A second install-skip-class incident occurs that installed client hooks would have blocked.
GitHub ships required checks compatible with direct pushes (no PR flow) - watch push-rules / merge-queue evolution.
Agent push cadence falls below ~5/day, making PR-flow latency immaterial.

constraints_honored.prop_051_disaster_class_review: See analysis.q4_fail_open and study Q4 - the 2026-05-21 recovery path itself is the canonical case that strict server enforcement would have blocked.
